questions.question: What does HLL stand for in computing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__High-Level Language__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Computer programming languages** are broadly categorized into** 2 types namely** – **High-Level Language and Low-Level Language.**
 
• **The abbreviation for High-Level Language is HLL and Low-Level Language is LLL.**
 
• **A high-level language (HLL) **is a programming language such as **C, FORTRAN, or Pascal** that enables a programmer to write programs that are more or less independent of a particular type of computer.
 
• Such languages are considered **high-level because** **they are closer to human languages** and further from **machine languages.**

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lisp, Prolog, Python, and R **are the main **AI programming languages** that are best suited for development and design for different kinds of software.
 
• **C language** is **developed **by **Dennis M. Ritchie** in the early 1970s.
 
• **Father of Computer** - Charles Babbage
 
• **Mother of Computer** - Ada Lovelace
 
• **The first computer programming** language was **created in 1883 by Ada Lovelace.**

questions.question: Lines joining places located at equal travel time from a common centre are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**isochrones.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isobronts **- A line drawn through geographical points at which a given phase of thunderstorm activity occurred simultaneously.
 
• **Isohaline **- These are the lines (or contours) that join points of equal salinity in an aquatic system. 
 
• **Isochrones **-Lines joining places located at the equal travel time from a common centre

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Iso-Seismal Line **- An isoseismal (line) is a contour or line on map bounding points of equal intensity fo.r a particular earthquake.
 
• **Home-Seismal Line** - Line on the Earth's surface connecting points where the seismic wave arrives, generated by an earthquake, at the same time.
 
• **Seismic gap** - It is a gap of places in a seismic zone where no earthquake occurs.
 
• **Isogonal line** - It is a line joining places with the same magnetic declination.

questions.question: Maps showing natural feature of the earth such as mountains, plateaus, rivers, plains, oceans, etc. are known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Relief Map__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A raised-relief map** or **terrain model** is a three-dimensional representation, **usually of terrain**, materialized as a **physical artefact.**
 
• When representing terrain, **the vertical dimension** is usually **exaggerated by a factor between five and ten.**
 
• This facilitates the **visual recognition** of **terrain features.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Political Map** - A Political Map represents countries, states, and towns. Often they are painted in different colours so we can see them better. This map shows names and boundaries.
 
• **Topographic Map** - Topography concerns the shape and character of the Earth's surface, and maps were among the first artefacts to record these observations.
 
• **Thematic Map** - A thematic map is a type of map that portrays the geographic pattern of a particular subject matter (theme) in a geographic area like temperature, language, or population.

Source:

https://ncert.nic.in/ncerts/l/fess204.pdf

questions.question: Who among the following did Babur defeat in the year 1528 at Chanderi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Medni Rai__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Battle of Chanderi** took place in the aftermath of the **Battle of Khanwa** in which the Mughal Emperor **Babur had defeated the Rajput Confederacy** and firmly established **Mughal rule.**
 
• **Babur** decided to **isolate the Rana** by inflicting a military defeat on one of his vassals **Medini Rai** who was the **ruler of Malwa.**
 
• Consequently, in December 1527, taking a circumlocutious route **Babur marched to the fortress of Chanderi** in **Malwa **which was the capital of the kingdom of **Malwa**.
 
• Upon reaching Chanderi, on** 20 January 1528**, Babur offered Shamsabad to **Medini Rai in exchange for Chanderi** as a peace overture but **the offer was rejected by Rai.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The second battle of Panipat - 5 November 1556
 
• The third battle of Panipat - 14 January 1761
 
• Battle of Khanwa - March 16, 1527.
 
• Battle of Halighati - 18 June 1576
 
• Battle of Buxar - 22/23 October 1764

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a scalar quantity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Torque__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Torque **is the measure of the **force **that can cause an object to **rotate about an axis.**
 
• **Force** is what causes an object to accelerate in** linear kinematics**.
 
• Similarly, **torque** is what causes an **angular acceleration**.
 
• Hence, torque can be defined as the **rotational equivalent of linear force.**
 
• Since **force needs** **direction **as well as **magnitude**.
 
• Therefore, it is a **vector quantity**. 
 
• Hence, **Torque is also a vector quantity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A quantity that has **magnitude **but no **particular direction** is described as a **scalar**.
 
• A quantity that has **magnitude and acts in a particular direction** is described as a **vector**.
 
• **Some vector quantities are **- Acceleration, Velocity, Force, etc.
 
• **Some Scalar quantities are** - Distance, time, temperature, Volume, Area, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT unicellular?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Spirogyra__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Spirogyra **(common names include **water silk**, mermaid's tresses, and blanket weed) is a filamentous charophyte **green alga** of the order **Zygnematales**, named for the helical or spiral arrangement of the **chloroplasts that is characteristic of the genus.**
 
• It is commonly found in **freshwater habitats**, and there are more than **400 species of Spirogyra in the world.**
 
• **Spirogyra **measures approximately** 10 to 100 μm** in width and may grow to **several centimetres in length.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**The characteristics of unicellular organisms are as follows:**__

 
• The unicellular organisms usually reproduce by **asexual means.**
 
• They can be **eukaryotes **or **prokaryotes**.
 
• They are found in almost **all habitats**, from **hot springs** to **frozen tundra**.
 
• They possess **whip-like structures** for movement.

questions.question: Which of the following viruses is responsible for causing influenza?

__
 
• **Myxovirus **can cause **Influenza** in humans.
 
• **Myxovirus **belongs to the **families Orthomyxoviridae** (agents of influenza) and **Paramyxoviridae**.
 
• There are two main types of influenza (flu) virus: **Types A and B.**
 
• **The influenza A and B viruses** that routinely **spread in people** (human influenza viruses) are **responsible for seasonal flu** epidemics each year.
 
• **Influenza A viruses** can be broken down into **sub-types depending** on the genes that make up the surface proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Smallpox - variola virus
 
• Polio - poliomyelitis
 
• Rabies - Lyssavirus 
 
• Mumps - paramyxovirus

questions.question: In which of the following countries was the first Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, the first programmable general-purpose electronic digital computer, developed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__United States of America__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ENIAC, in full Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer**, the first programmable general-purpose electronic digital computer, built during **World War II** by **the United States**.
 
• American physicist John Mauchly, American engineer J. Presper Eckert, Jr., and their colleagues at the Moore School of Electrical Engineering at the University of Pennsylvania led a government-funded project to build an all-electronic computer.
 
• Under contract to the **army and under the direction of Herman Goldstine**, work began in **early 1943 on ENIAC.**
 
• The next year, mathematician John von Neumann began frequent consultations with the group. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frontier **is the **fastest supercomputer** in the **World**.
 
• **The USA built the Frontier supercomputer**.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution are Indian citizens guaranteed the right to six fundamental freedoms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 19__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The heart of Article 19 says:** "Everyone has the **right to freedom** of **opinion and expression**, this right includes **freedom to hold opinions** without interference and to seek, receive and **impart information and ideas** **through any media and regardless of frontiers**."
 
• **Right to Freedom** is a **Fundamental Right** which is described under **Article 19 to 22.**
 
• **Article 19 gives freedom to:**__
 __
 
• Right to speech
 
• Right to Press
 
• Right to Silence
 
• Right to Information
 
• Right to move anywhere and reside anywhere
 
• Right to form Association and Union
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**Some important Borrowing of the Indian Constitution**__:

 
• **Fundamental Rights - USA**
 
• Fundamental Duties - Russia/USSR
 
• Election of President - Ireland
 
• **Concurrent list - Australia**
 
• Citizenship - Britain
 
• Republic - France
 
• Five year Plan - USSR/Russia
